title: First bebop record: Dizzy Gillespie's One Bass Hit
summary: He hears One Bass Hit on 78 outside a music store in Oneonta in the early fifties.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: What was the first bop record that you heard, or did you hear bop live first. How did it sort of enter?

The first bop record I ever heard was with my father when we went over to Oneonta, New York. In those days they used to have speakers outside of the music store playing the latest things, you know, that kind of thing. And we went in there, and I’ve still got the original 78. It was “One Bass Hit” by Dizzy Gillespie. And on one side was the big band version and on the other side was the small band version. And I’ve still got that 78. And I said, now that got my attention. That did get my attention. And that was the first one. But that would have been in the early 50’s as well and I hadn’t even started drums yet.
